summary: OpenAI published a case study describing how Model ML uses GPT-5.6 Sol in an agentic finance workflow to build PowerPoint decks and Excel workbooks, citing internal benchmark comparisons against Opus 5 and Fable 5.

practices.reason: Model ML's Composite evaluation methodology (assignment-to-deliverable scoring with professional-readiness gates and token efficiency) suggests a measurement approach for agentic document-generation tasks, though the benchmark itself is proprietary and unreplicated.
practices.quote: Its Composite evaluations follow an assignment from the initial finance brief through research and calculations to an editable deck or spreadsheet, then check the numbers, sources, formulas, and structure, as well as visual quality for presentations.

practices.reason: The described agent harness -- a core planning agent routing steps to the right model and tool, loading toolkits on demand, keeping the brief in context, and visually reviewing output before returning -- is a concrete scaffolding pattern, though tied to Model ML's own infrastructure.
practices.quote: Today, Model ML’s harness provides the agent with toolkits it can load to access data integrations, document editing tools and skills, and code execution environments.
